pr_body:
- The new API of Lucene provide a Weight#count function that can be used instead of shortcutTotalHitCount hack.
- I still have a test that fail (QueryPhaseTests => testrNumericSortOptimization), I will be happy to fix it if anyone give me some help on this one.
- Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/81034
pr_comment: I looked at some profiling-related failures. They indeed fail because we broke their expectations about how queries run. But there is also another problem, which is that because we now create the weight twice, we get two queries in the resulting profile: one for the weight we create to compute the hit count, and another one for the weight that gets created to feed the collector. It would be nice to have a single query in the response, either by actually only creating the weight once, or by collapsing the two entries in the resulting profile (e.g. could `AbstractInternalProfileTree#getProfileBreakdown` returns the same breakdown instance when passed the same query instance?). @javanna I'll need your help on this. :)
Thanks for the review, I will check later the other points when I can (failing test + query profile breakdown).

For reference I opened [LUCENE-10620](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/LUCENE-10620), which could help simplify this work by letting Lucene collectors optimize collection automatically thanks to `Weight#count`. The main benefit is that we would be creating the weight only once instead of once for the hit count and once for the collector, which in-turn would also help integration with profiling.

The above issue got merged and we recently upgraded Elasticsearch to a new Lucene snapshot that includes this change. This hopefully means that this change is no longer needed and that we could get rid of `shortcutTotalHitCount` entirely since it should be handled automatically by Lucene's `TotalHitCountCollector` now.

I opened #89047 to remove shortcutTotalHitCount. Thanks a lot for working with us @OlivierCavadenti , it was useful even if this PR did not get merged as it led us to finding a better way in lucene. Looking forward to your next contribution! I hope you don't mind if I close this PR.
